about: Adaptation evals for the learn skill on the 9.49 neural_circuit course. Each case is one /learn call in a fresh sandbox copy of .learn. Pairs share a topic and differ in phrasing, so depth/format should differ. Graded by the rubric; see run notes in evals/results/.

cases.question: In L08 the mixed fixed point of the reciprocal-inhibition WTA is a saddle. I get the eigenvalues -1±w from the Jacobian, but why exactly is the diagonal x1 = x2 its stable manifold, rather than some curved separatrix?
expect: answers the exact point directly: exchange symmetry makes x1=x2 invariant, and in the both-active region the dynamics are linear, so the stable eigenvector (1,1) spans a straight invariant line
does NOT re-teach nullclines, eigenvalues or WTA basics
short (a few paragraphs at most)
cites L08 (p.8-10)
math correct: Jacobian -I + [[0,-w],[-w,0]] has eigenvalue -1-w along (1,1) (stable) and w-1 along (1,-1) (unstable for w>1)

cases.question: I don't get the winner-take-all slide.
expect: either one probe question or a short layered answer ending in one probe; at most ONE question
intuition first then the formal model (profile: math = intuition AND formal)
uses the course model x1' = -x1 + [-w x2 + b1]_+ and cites L08 p.6-9
bridges to neuroscience (owl competitor suppression / decision-making) since that is the learner's strength
does not dump the full Lyapunov/Hopfield material

cases.question: Since all the eigenvalues of W have real part below 1, the network can't amplify its inputs, right? So non-normal amplification must need an unstable mode somewhere.
expect: corrects the premise FIRST and plainly: stable non-normal networks transiently amplify (or with input, have large steady gain) without any unstable mode
gives the mechanism: hidden feedforward structure via Schur form / non-orthogonal eigenvectors (L10)
a concrete example, ideally the 2-cell E-I or the practice-exam W2 with r1 exceeding 1
records a misconception (misc add) in the sandbox
cites L10 and/or the practice exam

cases.question: For W = [[w, -kw], [w, -kw]] in the non-normal lecture, where exactly does the feedforward weight w_ff = w(1+k) come from in the Schur form?
expect: direct derivation in the sum/difference (or Schur) basis: eigenvalues 0 and w(1-k), the off-diagonal Schur entry w(1+k)
math verified (SymPy or explicit algebra), no errors
concise; no re-teaching of what non-normality is
cites L10 NN p.12-17

cases.signal: asks about material beyond the current position
cases.question: How does the line attractor relate to the balanced state?
expect: notices the balanced state is introduced later (L09) than the current position (L05) and says so explicitly
answers with the minimum preview needed, framed as later material
anchors in what is in scope (L03-L05 line attractor, fine tuning)
does not silently use L09/L10 machinery as if known

cases.signal: correct vocabulary, asks for intuition (rusty math)
cases.question: What's the intuition for why the Fisher information of a Poisson neuron is f'^2/f?
expect: intuition AND formal per profile: signal slope f' vs Poisson noise variance f (variance = mean), J = slope^2 / variance
short derivation or pointer to it (L02 p.7, P1 problem 1)
peak-of-tuning-curve consequence (J=0 at the peak)
moderate length; does not assume fluent probability
